context:
Goal: 3D work that a cloud session can build and a reviewer can check.
Problem (goal): each choice sets the licence cost, where the work can run, and how a reviewer checks a scene, so the survey lane's next step depends on it.
Based on (read): the 3D tools survey lane found browser 3D (three.js with glTF models) is free and can be fully checked in a cloud container with no graphics card.
Based on (read): the same survey found Unity and Unreal need their editor open on your computer, and Unity needs a licence even when run without its window.
Departs from: main — adds a first 3D target.

Not blocking: the survey goes on; this sets what it plans next.

lastAnswer.note: Pick a, recorded by the coordinator at 12:35 CST from your note. The follow-up is item 277.

options.gain: Free, and cloud sessions can build and check it.
options.how: 3D that runs in a web page.
options.label: Browser 3D (three.js and glTF)
options.lose: No game-engine extras such as a scene editor or physics tools.

options.gain: A full engine at no cost.
options.label: Godot
options.lose: Cloud checks cover only the file structure; checking how a scene looks is not proven.

options.gain: The largest asset stores and tooling.
options.label: Unity or Unreal
options.lose: Licence cost, and the work runs only on your computer.

reply: Yes. Browser 3D is the only free option that a cloud session can both build and check by eye. Godot is free too, but the cloud can check only its file structure. So: a. Which page to port first is item 277.
title: What should your first 3D work be built in?
why: Free, and the cloud can build and check it end to end.
